Ben/Vivek —

Below is a proposed addendum text we can send to Novanet. I kept the language pragmatic and limited to measurable items (TPS, measurement window, burst policy, credits, and scaling lead time). Feel free to edit before we share.

--- PROPOSED RESERVED POOL TPS ASSURANCE ADDENDUM (DRAFT) ---
1. Definitions
- "Committed TPS": total sustained tokens/second guaranteed across the Customer's reserved pool as of the effective date. Measured as the rolling 5‑minute average across all serving nodes provisioned to the reserved pool.
- "Burst TPS": short-duration capacity above Committed TPS to absorb transient traffic spikes.

2. Commit and Burst
- Redwood Inference will guarantee a Committed TPS of 12,000 tokens/sec across Novanet's 24‑GPU reserved pool, effective on 2026-09-01.
- Customer may request up to three (3) Burst TPS events per calendar month, each not to exceed 15,000 tokens/sec and 15 minutes in duration. Burst events beyond these limits will be subject to on-demand billing at prevailing pay-as-you-go rates.

3. Measurement and SLO
- Availability SLO: 99.5% monthly availability for Committed TPS, where availability is defined as the percentage of 5‑minute measurement windows in which the rolling average throughput for the pool meets or exceeds 95% of Committed TPS.
- Incident measurement window: monthly. Baseline usage and throttling events will be analyzed from the platform's telemetry (time-series of rolling 5‑minute averages).

4. Remedies (Service Credits)
- If monthly availability falls below the SLO, Redwood will issue service credits calculated as: (SLO shortfall percentage) x (monthly reserved pool fee) x 0.5. Credits are capped at 50% of the monthly fee for any single month.

5. Mid‑term Capacity Additions and Billing
- Customer may elect to add up to 8 additional GPUs to the reserved pool during the term. Redwood requires 72 hours' notice for capacity provisioning and will pro-rate charges for the remainder of the billing period at the applicable reserved rate.
- If capacity is provisioned and Customer provides a written commitment to maintain the additional GPUs for at least 90 days, Redwood will apply a one-time onboarding credit representing 10% of the pro-rated monthly charge for the additional capacity to the next invoice.

6. Fallbacks and Degradation Policy
- In the event of sustained capacity constraints, Redwood will: (a) automatically route latency‑sensitive traffic to a quantized model variant with compatible output profile, (b) enable cross-region failover to an alternate reserved pool if configured, and (c) engage Customer's on-call contact. Failover/quantization may increase per-token latency or alter output characteristics; Redwood will notify Customer when fallbacks are used.

7. Reporting and Escalation
- Monthly TPS and latency reports will be provided via the Redwood Console and a shared Drive link. The parties will meet weekly for the first 30 days after any capacity addition to validate performance.

--- END DRAFT ---

I recommend we include the mutual_action_plan.docx with the timelines for provisioning and a short clause on procurement approvals. If you and Vivek sign off, I'll send this to Sara and procurement with the draft MAP and the HubSpot link.
